name: InfluxDB 3 (Core/Enterprise)
model: Tables (measurements) of tags, fields and time; line protocol writes; SQL and InfluxQL queries; embedded Python plugins
engine_note: Rust FDAP stack: Arrow in memory, DataFusion query engine, Parquet files on object storage or local disk; WAL flushed every second
consistency: No multi-row transactions. A write is acknowledged after the WAL is persisted (default flush every 1 s) unless no_sync is set; then it is queryable from an in-memory buffer; Parquet files written about every 10 minutes.
scaling: Core: one node, storage on object storage ('diskless'), tuned for recent data. Enterprise: multi-node with read replicas, high availability and compaction for long-range history.
licence: Core: MIT or Apache 2.0 (your choice); Enterprise: commercial licence

licence_events.event: InfluxDB 3 Core (MIT/Apache 2.0) and Enterprise (commercial) reach general availability, replacing the Go-based 1.x/2.x engine

version_note: 3.11.4, 3.11.3, 3.10.6 and 3.9.13 were all published 2026-09-08; 3.11.4 is the highest. Same version numbers cover Core and Enterprise.
reach: Reach for it for high-volume sensor, IoT or app metrics with many unique tag values, queried in SQL, with storage on cheap object storage.
avoid: Avoid if you need long-range history queries without Enterprise, joins with relational data, or the Prometheus ecosystem (PromQL, exporters) as your main interface.
escape: It ingests millions of points per second into compressed Parquet on object storage, beyond a Postgres table.
chat: Per-request latency and token metrics from the model-serving fleet, queried for dashboards.
notes: CLAIM CHECK (a) 'InfluxDB v3 is a Parquet and DataFusion engine': VERIFIED. README (https://github.com/influxdata/influxdb): 'powered by Apache Arrow, DataFusion, and Parquet'; 'Storage format: Apache Parquet on object storage (S3, Azure, GCP) or local disk'; 'Built with: Rust, Apache Arrow, DataFusion'. GA post (2025-04-15) names the 'FDAP stack' (Flight, DataFusion, Arrow, Parquet). More complete wording: Arrow in memory, DataFusion for queries, Parquet on disk/object storage. Durability doc quotes: 'If no_sync=false (default), the server sends a response to acknowledge the write' after the WAL flush; 'Every ten minutes (default), InfluxDB 3 Core persists the oldest data from the queryable buffer to the object store in Parquet format.' Licence quote: 'licensed under the permissive MIT or Apache 2 licenses at the user's choosing'. GA post: Enterprise adds 'compaction for long-range historical queries, high availability, multi-node clustering'. Note the fetch tool misreported the GA post date as 2026-09-30; page metadata says datePublished 2025-04-15. Managed offerings listed from memory of InfluxData products page (Cloud Serverless and Cloud Dedicated run the v3 engine), not re-fetched: unconfirmed. No Jepsen analysis.
